findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure via /ftp directory listing and stack traces
findings.description: The endpoint /ftp is publicly enumerable (CWE-200) and returns directory listings containing backup files (package.json.bak, package-lock.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx), acquisition notes, and other internal artifacts. Attempting to fetch disallowed extensions returns a verbose 500-style error including full stack trace, internal filesystem paths (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js), and Express middleware names. This information aids targeted exploitation.
steps: GET http://localhost:3000/ftp to enumerate directory contents
findings.evidence: Directory listing: ["quarantine","acquisitions.md","announcement_encrypted.md","coupons_2013.md.bak","eastere.gg","encrypt.pyc","incident-support.kdbx","legal.md","package-lock.json.bak","package.json.bak","suspicious_errors.yml"]. Error body: "Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" with stack trace including /juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js, /juice-shop/node_modules/express/lib/router/layer.js, and node:fs paths.

findings.title: Unauthenticated exposure of full application configuration and version
findings.description: Administrative endpoints /rest/admin/application-configuration and /rest/admin/application-version return full server configuration and exact application version without authentication (CWE-200, CWE-552). The JSON includes server settings, domain, social URLs, and likely secrets/keys further down in the response. This enables fingerprinting for known Juice Shop CVEs and reveals internal configuration.
findings.evidence: {"version":"19.2.1"} returned with HTTP 200. Configuration endpoint returns 21770 bytes containing server.port, baseUrl, domain, altcoinName, privacyContactEmail, chatBot settings, and continuing with likely secrets.

findings.title: Broken Access Control: /api/Users/ lists all users including admins without role verification
findings.description: Endpoint /api/Users/ returns the complete user database (CWE-284/CWE-639) when called with a standard customer JWT. The backend does not enforce admin role, allowing any authenticated user to enumerate all accounts, emails, roles, and profile metadata. This is a vertical/horizontal privilege escalation.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 with user list including admin@juice-sh.op (id:1, role:admin), jim@juice-sh.op (id:2, role:customer), bender@juice-sh.op (id:3, role:customer), bkimminich (id:4, role:admin), and more.

findings.title: SQL Injection in /rest/products/search?q= permits arbitrary database exfiltration
findings.description: The search endpoint concatenates user input directly into a SQLite query (CWE-89). A UNION SELECT with 9 columns maps Products schema to Users table, returning id, email, and password hash for every user. This is full database read and can be escalated to RCE via SQLite extensions or further manipulation.
steps: GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert')) UNION SELECT id, email, password, '4','5','6','7','8','9' FROM Users--
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 returned Users table: admin@juice-sh.op hash 0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500; jim@juice-sh.op hash e541ca7ecf72b8d1286474fc613e5e45; bender@juice-sh.op hash 0c36e517e3fa95aabf1bbffc6744a4ef; bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com hash 6edd9d726cbdc873c539e41ae8757b8c; etc.

findings.title: Mass Assignment: arbitrary user registration with role=admin
findings.description: The user creation endpoint /api/Users/ accepts and persists the role field sent by the client (CWE-915). An unauthenticated attacker can register a new account with role=admin, bypassing all authorization controls and obtaining full administrative privileges.
steps: POST /api/Users/ with JSON body including role: admin
findings.evidence: HTTP 201 returned new user id:24, email: adminclone2026@example.com, role: admin, profileImage: defaultAdmin.png.

findings.title: [ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: [ZAP] X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing
findings.description: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This allows older versions of Internet Explorer and Chrome to perform MIME-sniffing on the response body, potentially causing the response body to be interpreted and displayed as a content type other than the declared content type. Current (early 2014) and legacy versions of Firefox will use the declared content type (if one is set), rather than performing MIME-sniffing. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps:
Solução: Ensure that the application/web server sets the Content-Type header appropriately, and that it sets the X-Content-Type-Options header to 'nosniff' for all web pages.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session ID in URL Rewrite

findings.title: [ZAP] Re-examine Cache-control Directives
findings.description: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached. | CWE-525 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".

findings.title: [ZAP] Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797. | CWE-319 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session Management Response Identified
findings.description: The given response has been identified as containing a session management token. The 'Other Info' field contains a set of header tokens that can be used in the Header Based Session Management Method. If the request is in a context which has a Session Management Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the session management to use the tokens identified. | CWE--1 | WASC--1
steps: Solução: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: [ZAP] Application Error Disclosure
findings.description: This page contains an error/warning message that may disclose sensitive information like the location of the file that produced the unhandled exception. This information can be used to launch further attacks against the web application. The alert could be a false positive if the error message is found inside a documentation page. | CWE-550 | WASC-13

findings.title: [ZAP] Information Disclosure - Debug Error Messages
findings.description: The response appeared to contain common error messages returned by platforms such as ASP.NET, and Web-servers such as IIS and Apache. You can configure the list of common debug messages. | CWE-1295 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Disable debugging messages before pushing to production.

findings.title: [ZAP] Authentication Request Identified

If the request is in a context which has an Authentication Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the authentication to match the request identified. | CWE--1 | WASC--1
steps: Solução: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: [ZAP] CSP: Failure to Define Directive with No Fallback

steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is properly configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

action.description: Endpoint /api/Users/ returns the complete user database (CWE-284/CWE-639) when called with a standard customer JWT. The backend does not enforce admin role, allowing any authenticated user to enumerate all accounts, emails, roles, and profile metadata. This is a vertical/horizontal privilege escalation.
action.evidence: HTTP 200 with user list including admin@juice-sh.op (id:1, role:admin), jim@juice-sh.op (id:2, role:customer), bender@juice-sh.op (id:3, role:customer), bkimminich (id:4, role:admin), and more.

steps.observation:

action.title: SQL Injection in /rest/products/search?q= permits arbitrary database exfiltration
action.description: The search endpoint concatenates user input directly into a SQLite query (CWE-89). A UNION SELECT with 9 columns maps Products schema to Users table, returning id, email, and password hash for every user. This is full database read and can be escalated to RCE via SQLite extensions or further manipulation.
steps: GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert')) UNION SELECT id, email, password, '4','5','6','7','8','9' FROM Users--

steps.thought: Cobertura: já tenho Sensitive Data Exposure, Broken Access Control, Injection. Agora preciso tocar XSS, Mass Assignment, SSRF, JWT flaws, Path Traversal, Business Logic, etc. Vou testar Mass Assignment via /api/Users/ (PUT no próprio perfil setando role=admin).

O token JWT fornecido retorna 401 em PUT — possivelmente expirado ou assinatura OpenSSL não suportada. Vou tentar fazer login para obter token novo. Primeiro verifico se o login funciona com credenciais conhecidas (o hash de jim é e541ca...). Mas não sei a senha. Vou usar forgot-password ou login comum. Antes disso, testar endpoints sem auth.

JWT novo obtido. Vou testar Mass Assignment novamente com este token, tentando alterar role para admin no próprio perfil.

O servidor parece ter problema de validação de JWT (algoritmo RS256 com OpenSSL). Isso pode ser uma vulnerabilidade JWT em si. Vou decodificar o JWT e testar variantes: alg=none, HS256 com chave pública, etc. Primeiro, vou testar sem assinatura (alg=none).

O GET /rest/basket/6 funciona com novo token. O PUT /api/Users/23 dá erro de OpenSSL. Isso pode ser porque PUT usa middleware de autenticação diferente ou há bug. Vou testar PUT com payload vazio/simples e outros métodos.

GET funciona, PUT dá erro OpenSSL. Isso pode ser um bug no middleware de autorização do PUT. Vou testar com header Authorization formatado de outra forma, ou testar se é problema no token antigo vs novo. Também testar Mass Assignment via POST /api/Users/ com role=admin.
Mass Assignment CRITICAL confirmado: registrando usuário com role=admin diretamente via POST /api/Users/. Vou reportar.

action.title: Mass Assignment: arbitrary user registration with role=admin
action.description: The user creation endpoint /api/Users/ accepts and persists the role field sent by the client (CWE-915). An unauthenticated attacker can register a new account with role=admin, bypassing all authorization controls and obtaining full administrative privileges.
steps: POST /api/Users/ with JSON body including role: admin
action.evidence: HTTP 201 returned new user id:24, email: adminclone2026@example.com, role: admin, profileImage: defaultAdmin.png.
